svg.title: RecLoop system architecture
svg.desc: System architecture of RecLoop. The store (Next.js) and the shopping assistant (FastAPI, Claude) call the Go api. A recommendation request runs five stages inside one 100 ms budget: user context from Redis; recall from SASRec through the gRPC model server, ItemCF, popularity and generated items; weighted RRF fusion and filters; LightGBM ranking through the model server; and a second-price ad auction with budgets and frequency caps. The api reads and writes PostgreSQL with pgvector, a Redis instance for state and one for cache, and publishes events to Redpanda. Stream consumers apply each event once: the aggregator updates the user state, the log sink stores events in PostgreSQL and billing writes the charge ledger. A near-line worker runs MiniOneRec and writes generated items to Redis. Offline, a Spark job joins training samples from the event log, training produces a versioned bundle, and a release goes through validation and a 5 percent canary before the model server serves it. It runs on Docker Compose and on Kubernetes with Helm, HPA and KEDA, observed with Prometheus, Grafana and OpenTelemetry. A pulse follows a request, then a click event, then the offline loop.
svg.text: gRPC deadlines · circuit breakers · degrade, never fail
STREAM CONSUMERS · each event applied once
